These are the 10 I judged most likely true. The first four rest on graph structure: an edit has almost no effect when the edge's path to the output is cut, so its effect is lower than when the path is intact. The other six rest on the expectation that filling an empty edge with a conv gains more than swapping one existing op for another. That is most dependable for edges 0 and 5, the sole routes into node 1 and into the output, and weaker for edges 1 and 4, which have alternative paths. I did not run any benchmark data to check these.
